utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, we will now see that this statement abounds in names of people from that list that the witness calls accomplices, and it's clear that this contradicts the allegation that people were brought in and arrested arbitrarily. This is an Official Note. This is not a statement. It's an official document of the police and can be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you not put the question without putting the document first?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I already have, your Excellencies. I asked on what basis people were arrested, and the witness said that one arrested person talks about others and then the others are brought in. This Official Note is a perfect example of that procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Never mind where he sent his family. Let's look at the next page. And without reading the whole text, please just look at the names he mentions of people who were his accomplices, policemen: Besim Mirkic, Nihad Sivac, Hamdija Kahrimanovic, Hamdija A Lukic, Mirsad Susic. The whole page is filled with names, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is dated March 1993. I don't see the relevance to the questions. This witness has said he was in security, he wasn't an operative, so I just think it's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he was caught several times and escaped several times, and he's talking here about events from before the war. He begins with February 1992 and enumerates a large number of names, and here we see the names of the most prominent people who were arrested later on these grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the Chamber agrees with Ms. Sutherland. Please move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, maybe Dr. Karadzic hasn't said exactly what the object is. But it seems to me that if you understood it, you would see that it's relevant and arises from the examination. So Dr. Karadzic is charged, with among other things, unlawful detentions of people who are in that camp, and he's attempting to show that people in that camp -- in fact, people who are registered as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, he should have done that in his direct examination. It does not arise from her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, in her cross-examination, as I think Dr. Karadzic already picked up on, she indicated that there was some question as to whether people were arbitrarily arrested and put in that camp. Now Dr. Karadzic is addressing that by showing that the very people who were supposed to have been arbitrarily arrested, they had information on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was just in relation to summarising what he was convicted of. I didn't go into it in any detail at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did his indictment cover the period of this, March of 1993, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's certainly not the case that was Rule 11 bis'd from here. It was from April till December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: This note speaks of -- you can see the date of February 1992, March -- excuse me, May 19th 1992, so the fact that the statement was taken in March of 1993 doesn't make any difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's from the 30th of April 1992 to the end of 1992, the Bosnian indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have separate point, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President, I'm sorry, in response to what Mr. Robinson said, as long as we are all on our feet. This document was -- there's a bait and switch going on. Now, Mr. Karadzic offered this to show the nature, the allegedly not arbitrary nature of the procedures involved that resulted in the incarceration of people in 1992. Now he's -- wants to apparently use a 1993 document that obviously can't bear on the procedures used in 1992, it couldn't have been part of that procedure at the time and rendered it non-arbitrary, but he wants to use some of the substance of that to justify, belatedly justify any incarceration which has nothing to do with the arbitrariness of the procedure at the time which was the original point for its purported admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just respond to that. If this document was dated 2013, it would still -- and it said that the people were in that camp had been arrested for good reason, that would still be relevant. It's just a question of the weight. So I don't understand Mr. Tieger's point, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we see the first page again of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: If it could be lifted, I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to make the point, I didn't question in cross-examination any questions about the arbitrariness or not of people coming to the camp.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Learned Madam Sutherland asked on page 18, line 12, whether the witness, Mr. Mejakic, agrees or confirms that the court in Bosnia had found that, among other things, people had been brought in arbitrarily. He agreed that was written in the judgement. He didn't agree that that's the way it happened. But he declined to comment on the judgement. I think it would be prejudicial to leave things as they are currently in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I see the imprisonment which was the arbitrary and unlawful confinement of camp detainees, that passage. But I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here on the first page, does it say what they did on 19th May, 23rd May? Can we scroll up a bit?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: May I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to help clear up one thing. In the second paragraph of this Official Note, it says the interview was conducted concerning the circumstances of the commission of crimes in the area of Prijedor municipality in the course of 1992, and the interviewee states the following, then he speaks about how he sent his family into safety and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we find here when this interview was conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, your Excellencies. On 12th of March 1993, but it talks about 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber has given its ruling. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many names are mentioned here, are these names familiar to you, and was this sufficient reason for these people to be brought in and interrogated?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: There are really a lot of names here, some are familiar, others are not, but judging by the experience of police operatives, these were sufficient grounds to bring in and question these people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page? Can we see the box?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know about this captain, Cerkez Sead?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: That's a former JNA officer, if I'm not mistaken. He was the commander of all the armed forces in the area of Kozarac and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this box, do you see any names of people who were brought in and interrogated in the investigating centres of Prijedor? Do you know any of these names?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Give me a moment. I know a lot of these surnames and some people with these surnames were detained down there, but I cannot be completely sure that any of these had been brought to Omarska and then released. But there is evidence, and even video footage, showing people who managed to get hold of weapons and flee to Croatia, gave statements there, claimed that they had been in Omarska, then transferred to Trnopolje, from Trnopolje they travelled to Croatia, et cetera. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page? It says the previous page towards the bottom, I'll read it out. It says: [As read] "Hamdija decided to take the road Prijedor-Banja Luka, the old road, to wait for the first passing vehicle and kill whoever is in it. Everybody went except Ismet and I. The two of us remained among the plum trees 100 metres away. I had a rifle, Ismet had none. I hear the car coming but I can't see it. And then we heard volleys of fire." We see later from the text that the car had burned. And then it says: [As read] "After this, we went home to Ismet Besic, and then Hamdija suggested that we torch Bozo Indzic's house." Do you know this man, Bozo Indzic, and what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Bozo Indzic, who was an elderly man at the time, and his family, one of the few Serbian families who lived in that area overlooking Kozarac, from what I know, from other people, I don't know it directly, that house was burnt and the family of Bozo Indzic was killed. There was a series of similar incidents where people got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the end of this paragraph, it says he had heard from Mustafa Haliphagic [phon], his son, and somebody called Zilho [phon] that in Kamicani they had assaulted a tractor and killed one man. Can you tell the Chamber until what time and what kind of danger such groups posed to the citizens?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: I happened to know the victim in this incident. It's not one man. It's two people, one of them is Marko Dakic, a civilian, and all the way up to mid-1993, similar groups around Mount Kozara were a great danger to the citizenry, not only to the Serbs but the Muslims as well. And these renegade groups or extremists, what shall I call them, were operative all the way up to the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I tender this document for identification while we await for translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives MFI number D4141, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just show one more document on the ELMO and that would be the end. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is and when it was done?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note of the public security station Bosanski Novi, dated 9 June 1992, done on the same day, 9 June, on the basis of an interview conducted with Sead Halagic [phon] from Prijedor who was arrested and brought in to the public security station of Bosanski Novi on 8 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For the parties in the list, number 05519, Sead Halagic is the first name on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that on the list of people in the first category.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you assist us with this? He mentions Hambarine, Carakovo, Kurjevo Brdo, and the groups that were there. Is this consistent with what you knew about these localities and the groups active there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is his account of everything that preceded the war, people organising themselves, Jama is mentioned here, Kotska, Slavko Ecimovic, some groups like Garavi Sokak, Kemo Divljak is mentioned although his last name is really Alagic, Kurjevo forest is mentioned, and I think this is about the preparation for the attack of 31st May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the last page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Biscani is mentioned also, Ljubija, Kurjevo, Biscani. Let's see the last page. Did you know anything about Brisevo village? Were there any groups there? Was Brisevo attacked without any reason or was there perhaps a reason?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Brisevo is a bit further away from Omarska, quite a way, and I have no particular knowledge about that village. I believe it was populated mainly by Croats. I think. But I have no knowledge really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this doesn't arise from my cross-examination, Brisevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Leave it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this Boro Bukva, who is he, the person who drafted this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MEJAKIC
utterances.text: Boro Bukva is a policeman in the public security station of Novi Grad, that is Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I also tender this document. I have more but I won't use them because we have no more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At the moment it does not have a 65 ter number, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D4142, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mejakic for your testimony and for the efforts you made here. On behalf of the Defence. I suppose the other parties will thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Reid informs me it's 1D02974.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does it have an English translation? No. On behalf of the Chamber, Mr. Mejakic, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. You are free to go. Thank for your assistance, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless there is anything, we will adjourn until Tuesday morning. The hearing is adjourned.
